correctness.rationale: The source's exact centered radial SDE and exact diffusivity were reconstructed under the stated hypotheses. The logarithmic time change gives the time-homogeneous coefficient \(\bar a(y)=A y^{2-q}(C-\kappa y^q)\). Applying the \(q\)-power map gives diffusion variance \(2K u(1-u)\) and drift \(K\{\alpha-(\alpha+\eta)u\}\), with all constants reduced exactly. The potentially singular second derivative at the origin when \(1<q<2\) is canceled by the source's exact \(y^{2-q}\) degeneracy, so smooth approximation justifies Itô's formula. Braun's self-similar marginal transforms exactly to \(\operatorname{Beta}(\alpha,\eta)\). The correlation formula follows from the linear drift and a bounded square-integrable martingale term, not from simulation or an unproved transition formula.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a one-time self-similar marginal statement to a complete classical path-law identification for a natural scalar observable. It shows that, under only the weak-solution hypotheses used by Braun, the normalized centered radial power is an ordinary reversible Markov diffusion with explicit Beta equilibrium and exact two-time power-law correlation. This supplies transition-level structure unavailable from the source's marginal scaling statement or stopped estimates and gives a direct route to the full Jacobi toolkit for this nonlinear process. The object and transform are canonical: the power is forced by the Barenblatt exponent and exactly linearizes the radial diffusivity.
